Session FRI-0-1-B : Sparsity in hyperspectral data processing                                                                 86

**MAPPING BENTHIC SUBSTRATE COVERAGE AND BATHYMETRY USING BIO-OPTICAL MODELLING - AN EN-MAP CASE STUDY IN THE COASTAL WATERS OF HELGOLAND**

Katja Dörnhöfer and Natascha Oppelt,  
*Kiel University, Department of Geography, Ludewig-Meyn-Straße 14, 24098 Kiel*

**Abstract :** Kelp forests, which are dense stands of brown seaweeds of the taxonomic order Laminariales, often are used as indicator species for assessing the environmental state of coastal waters. To this end, large scale monitoring approaches are required apart from traditional labor-intensive point sampling techniques. Bio-optical modelling with hyperspectral remote sensing data provides the possibility to take on the task. Yet, hyperspectral imagery mainly originates from airborne data. Within in the scope of the EnMAP Preparatory Program the bio-optical model WASI-2D was tested to the coastal area of Helgoland. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Aquatic Ecology and Coastal Habitat Assessment

1
Terminal Report for the Participatory Resource and Socio-Economic Assessment of Butuan Bay Project

The Photo Transect Method was used to estimate benthic lifeform cover. Benthic lifeforms are
category names for groups of plants and animals present in the coastal area or reef. This was done by
a SCUBA diver taking a photograph of benthic communities every one meter along a 50m transect line.
Underwater images were digitally processed using the Coral Point Count with Excel extension (CPCe;
Kohler and Gill, 2006) at 10 random points per image. Identification of corals and other invertebrates
was based on Veron (1993), CoralId software (2000) and Colin and Arneson (1995).
Associated reef fishes were assessed using the daytime Fish Visual Census (FVC) described in
English et al. (1997). Using the same transect line for benthic assessment, an observer recorded the fish
species, including size estimates and counts within the 5-m perimeter on both sides of the 50m transect
